analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the impact of nationwide surveillance and control measures during a large measles outbreak in Bangladesh, 2026, and to identify factors contributing to the persistence of transmission despite high vaccine coverage.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study conducted nationwide surveillance in Bangladesh from April 2 to May 27, 2026, across 8 administrative divisions, identifying 67,079 suspected and 8,834 confirmed measles cases.
analysis.methods: The study relied on reported data from surveillance systems and public health records to assess the outbreak's scale, identify contributing factors, and evaluate the effectiveness of control measures.
analysis.main_results: Among suspected cases, 472 deaths were reported, and 88 deaths were reported among confirmed cases. Transmission continued despite high reported vaccine coverage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings highlight the challenges in measles control, even with high vaccine coverage, and suggest that vaccine stockouts, discontinued campaigns, and coverage overestimation may have played a significant role in the outbreak.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results inform the need for improved vaccine distribution, sustained vaccination campaigns, and accurate coverage monitoring to prevent future outbreaks and reduce measles-related mortality.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by reliance on reported data, which may be subject to underreporting or inaccuracies, and the lack of direct laboratory confirmation for all cases. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed the nationwide measles outbreak in Bangladesh during April 2 to May 27, 2026, identifying 67,079 suspected and 8,834 confirmed cases. Among suspected cases, 472 deaths were reported, and 88 deaths were reported among confirmed cases. Despite high reported vaccine coverage, transmission persisted, likely due to vaccine stockouts, discontinued campaigns, and coverage overestimation. The findings emphasize the importance of reliable vaccine distribution and continuous surveillance to prevent future outbreaks. The study's reliance on reported data introduces potential limitations, reducing the strength of the evidence to moderate.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在评估2026年孟加拉国大规模麻疹暴发期间全国范围内的监测及控制措施的影响,并确定尽管疫苗覆盖率较高,传播仍持续存在的因素。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究在2026年4月2日至5月27日间,对孟加拉国8个行政区域进行了全国范围的监测,发现了67,079例疑似病例和8,834例确诊病例。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究依赖于监测系统和公共卫生记录中报告的数据,以评估暴发的规模、确定相关因素,并评估控制措施的有效性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在疑似病例中报告了472例死亡,在确诊病例中报告了88例死亡。尽管报告的疫苗覆盖率较高,传播仍持续存在。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果突显了在麻疹防控中面临的挑战,即使具有高疫苗覆盖率,也表明疫苗短缺、中止的活动以及覆盖率高估可能在暴发中发挥了重要作用。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些结果强调了改进疫苗分发、持续疫苗接种活动以及准确监测覆盖率的必要性,以防止未来的暴发并减少与麻疹相关的死亡率。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究受限于依赖报告数据,这些数据可能存在低估或不准确的情况,且所有病例均未进行直接实验室确认。由于这些限制,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Measles coinfection in an unvaccinated adolescent with secondary pulmonary TB - a case report.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Romania records the highest tuberculosis incidence in the European Union (44.3 per 100,000 inhabitants) and accounts for 77.8% of EU measles cases (1,447 per million inhabitants). Lack of vaccination remains the key determinant of both epidemics. CASE PRESENTATION: A 17-year-old unvaccinated female from a rural area presented with serologically confirmed measles during the intensive phase of antituberculous treatment for extensive secondary pulmonary tuberculosis with polyserositis. The diagnosis of tuberculosis had been established by positive AFB smear (2+ and 4+) and Xpert MTB/RIF molecular testing. Measles was confirmed by the pathognomonic clinical triad (generalised micro-maculopapular rash, Koplik's spots, conjunctival hyperaemia) and positive anti-measles IgM serology. The clinical course was marked by measles-induced immunosuppression, hepatotoxicity (ALT 156 U/L; AST 131 U/L), thrombocytopenia (platelets 122 × 103/μL), leukopenia (WBC 3.65 × 103/μL), and worsening of pre-existing cavitary pulmonary lesions on serial chest CT. CONCLUSION: Measles-tuberculosis coinfection in an unvaccinated adolescent represents a complex clinical emergency with significant multisystem morbidity. MMR and BCG vaccination, active community screening, and directly observed therapy (DOT) remain the indispensable pillars of prevention.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to highlight the clinical complexity of measles-tuberculosis coinfection in an unvaccinated adolescent, given the high tuberculosis incidence and measles cases in Romania. The background underscores the role of vaccination in preventing these diseases.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This case report describes a 17-year-old unvaccinated female from a rural area who presented with measles during the intensive phase of antituberculous treatment for secondary pulmonary tuberculosis with polyserositis. The study was conducted in Romania.
analysis.methods: The diagnosis of measles was confirmed through serological testing and the pathognomonic clinical triad. Tuberculosis was diagnosed using AFB smear and Xpert MTB/RIF molecular testing. The clinical course was monitored through laboratory tests and serial chest CT scans.
analysis.main_results: Measles was confirmed by the presence of a generalised micro-maculopapular rash, Koplik's spots, conjunctival hyperaemia, and positive anti-measles IgM serology.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the case as a complex clinical emergency, highlighting the significant multisystem morbidity associated with measles-tuberculosis coinfection in an unvaccinated adolescent. This case adds to the understanding of the clinical challenges posed by such coinfections.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings underscore the importance of vaccination in preventing measles and tuberculosis, and the need for active community screening and directly observed therapy to manage such coinfections effectively.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a single case report, which limits the generalisability of the findings. However, the evidence is strong due to the clear clinical and laboratory confirmation of both infections.

analysis.summary_en: This case report describes a 17-year-old unvaccinated female from Romania who presented with measles during the intensive phase of treatment for secondary pulmonary tuberculosis with polyserositis. Measles was confirmed by serological testing and the pathognomonic clinical triad, while tuberculosis was diagnosed using AFB smear and Xpert MTB/RIF molecular testing. The clinical course was marked by measles-induced immunosuppression and worsening of pre-existing pulmonary lesions. The authors interpret this as a complex clinical emergency with significant multisystem morbidity. The findings highlight the importance of vaccination and active community screening in preventing and managing measles-tuberculosis coinfections. The study's limitations include its single-case design, which restricts generalisability, but the evidence is strong due to the clear diagnostic confirmation.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在突出未接种疫苗的青少年中麻疹与结核病合并感染的临床复杂性,鉴于罗马尼亚结核病发病率和麻疹病例数均较高。背景强调了疫苗接种在预防这些疾病中的作用。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本病例报告描述了一名17岁的未接种疫苗的农村女性,在进行抗结核治疗的强化治疗阶段时,因麻疹而就诊。该研究在罗马尼亚进行。
elements_zh.methods: 通过血清学检测和特征性临床三联征确认了麻疹的诊断。结核病通过抗酸杆菌涂片和Xpert MTB/RIF分子检测进行诊断。通过实验室检测和连续胸部CT扫描监测了临床过程。
elements_zh.main_results: 麻疹通过全身性斑丘疹、科普利克斑、结膜充血以及阳性抗麻疹 IgM血清学检测得到确认。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将该病例解释为一种复杂的临床紧急情况,强调了未接种疫苗的青少年中麻疹与结核病合并感染所导致的显著多系统发病率。该病例为理解此类合并感染带来的临床挑战提供了新的认识。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果突显了疫苗接种在预防麻疹和结核病中的重要性,并强调了主动社区筛查和直接观察治疗对于有效管理此类合并感染的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究是一项单一的病例报告,这限制了研究结果的普遍适用性。然而,由于两种感染的临床和实验室确认明确,证据是强有力的。

analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究是一项单一的病例报告,这限制了研究结果的普遍适用性。然而,由于两种感染的临床和实验室确认明确,证据是强有力的。

papers.title: Why historical data matter for understanding the long-term effects of measles
papers.abstract: Although measles prevention is well understood, there remains a contested area of study pertaining to how the measles virus affects the immune system and mortality in the months to years following infection 1 . Studies on the long-term consequences of measles remain essential to our understanding of the full impact of measles and the other infectious diseases it intensifies. This is particularly relevant in light of recent global outbreaks, which suggest that the WHO goal of measles elimination by 2030 is unlikely to be achieved 2 . Measles therefore remains a potentially fatal infection with further-reaching implications for global health.Studies on how measles affect the immune system have produced inconsistent results when describing the length of the immune amnesia effect, as well as its overall impact on the infectious disease mortality, with some suggesting that up to half of all childhood infectious disease mortality in the pre-vaccine era is related to measles immune effects 3 . Much of the difficulty of studying the impact of measles-induced immune amnesia stems from the inherent unequal distribution of measles infections. In an observational setting, natural measles cases in high income countries are often strongly confounded by variables such as pre-existing comorbidities, and healthcare-seeking behaviors. In the post-vaccination era, the extreme rarity of measles cases ensures that the few individuals who do contract the virus are inherently unrepresentative of the broader population, introducing significant selection bias into observational studies. Alternatively, in high burden populations where measles is more common, there persists inequalities in healthcare access which complicates the establishment of reliable cohorts. Working within these restraints, studies have looked at quantifying the increased risk in non-measles infections post-measles-infection, when compared to children who were not sick with measles 4,5 . However, these studies using contemporary individual data cannot link immune amnesia to mortality due to limited cohort sizes and low mortality rates. The claim that measles immune amnesia may have contributed to up to half of all childhood deaths from infectious diseases in the pre-vaccine era, and that following the introduction of vaccination, the subsequent decline in measles infections was the primary driver of reduced childhood infectious disease mortality comes from a paper by Mina et al. These authors measured measles immune amnesia by quantifying the drop in non-measles infectious disease mortality in three countries before and after the introduction of the measles vaccines. This statement does not address mortality fluctuations across history and regions, but in the case of Denmark, the data used to make this claim, comes from when infectious disease mortality was already nearing historic lows. In 1986, the year before the measles vaccine was introduced, there were a total of 19 deaths from non-measles childhood infections, five years later, in 1991, there was a total of 16 deaths. This makes the results from Mina et al. 3 unsuitable for speculating on the contribution of measles immune amnesia to childhood infectious disease death in the pre-vaccine era, because by the 1980s, many of the most significant contributors to infectious disease mortality had been largely eradicated.This claim is also inconsistent with broad trends in historic measles infections and mortality rates. For example, in the early 20 th century in Copenhagen, census data shows childhood mortality is highly concentrated towards the first year of life 6 , well before the average age of measles infection which was estimated to be 5.65 years 7 using weekly measles infection numbers taken from 1907 to 1930. To visualize this, Figure 1 shows the age distribution of measles infections and the non-measles deaths per 10'000 by age. The distribution of deaths from measles and other infectious diseases comes from an annual report on epidemic diseases in Copenhagen from 1911 and shown in Table 1.-Table 1 here -A fitted gamma and power-law function were used to visualize the overall trend. The trend produced by measles infection counts were similar to those produced by simulations from Metcalf et al. 7 .The lack of overlap between the distributions makes it unlikely that measles immune amnesia was a significant contributor to infectious disease mortality in 20 th historicCopenhagen, but more research needs to be done on studying infectious disease mortality at the individual level to better understand its impact on the pre-vaccine infectious disease landscape.-Figure 1 here -We propose that historic data offers a unique set of advantages for studying how measles infections affect the immune system and when estimating the overall impact of measles immune amnesia on historic and contemporary mortality. Data from countries like Denmark and Switzerland have well-preserved, individual-level historic mortality data and morbidity data from a pre-vaccination period long before the first vaccine was introduced. Data from an era which mortality was still high offers a valuable opportunity to investigate how measles infections increase susceptibility to other infectious diseases and increase mortality postinfection. We are, of course, aware that analyzing measles dynamics through pre-vaccination historical data presents a distinct set of methodological challenges. Due to the pathogen's very high transmissibility, infection was almost universal among individuals who lived long enough.Consequently, although the infected cohorts are highly representative of the general population, the ubiquity of the disease makes it impossible to establish a reliable control group of individuals who were not exposed to the virus. However, because the timing of historical measles outbreaks has been well documented through historical demographic research, study designs analogous to those conducted using contemporary data can also be reconstructed for historical populations. Moreover, detailed historical measles case and hospital records often remain available in the archives and can be linked to death certificates, enabling individuallevel analyses of the long-term consequences of measles infection.Moreover, an added benefit of studying historical data of the pre-vaccine era, is that it decouples it from the theory commonly referred to as 'non-specific vaccine effects' (NSE) which states that live attenuated vaccines provide non-specific benefits to the immune system which decrease all-cause mortality in vaccinated individuals 8 . Although the theory of NSE has not become universally accepted, it exists within this discourse as an alternative explanation for the correlation between measles suppression and reduced all-cause mortality. By studying the association of measles infections and non-measles mortality prior to the availability of measles vaccines, we can more confidently attribute the effect to measles immune amnesia, rather than NSE.This paradigm once again illustrates the importance of historical demography and historical epidemiology and highlights the value of international networks such as this COST Action "CA22116 -The Great Leap. Multidisciplinary approaches to health inequalities, 1800-2022" 9 . To understand the long-term consequences of infectious diseases such as measles and the phenomenon of immune amnesia, contemporary data alone are not sufficient. Even studies directly comparing vaccinated and unvaccinated children are often affected by substantial confounding, as the two groups may differ systematically with respect to socioeconomic status, access to healthcare, health-seeking behavior, and parental attitudes towards healthcare and vaccination. Integrating historical data is therefore essential to overcome these limitations and to advance our understanding of measles-induced immune amnesia and its long-term consequences.Annual counts of measles infections were reported in four age brackets; under 1, 1-5, 5-15, and 15-65. These totals were fitted to a gamma distribution to show the overall trend.Mortality data was in higher granularity with yearly frequency up until age 5, and then 5-10, 10-15, and 10-20. These totals were fitted with a power law function to show the overall trend. Notably, "infant diarrhea", the most significant source of mortality among under 1s at 286.6 per 10,000 was not included in the death total because it is considered food and water borne.

Studies on the long-term consequences of measles remain essential to our understanding of the full impact of measles and the other infectious diseases it intensifies. This is particularly relevant in light of recent global outbreaks, which suggest that the WHO goal of measles elimination by 2030 is unlikely to be achieved 2 . Measles therefore remains a potentially fatal infection with further-reaching implications for global health.Studies on how measles affect the immune system have produced inconsistent results when describing the length of the immune amnesia effect, as well as its overall impact on the infectious disease mortality, with some suggesting that up to half of all childhood infectious disease mortality in the pre-vaccine era is related to measles immune effects 3 . Much of the difficulty of studying the impact of measles-induced immune amnesia stems from the inherent unequal distribution of measles infections. In an observational setting, natural measles cases in high income countries are often strongly confounded by variables such as pre-existing comorbidities, and healthcare-seeking behaviors. In the post-vaccination era, the extreme rarity of measles cases ensures that the few individuals who do contract the virus are inherently unrepresentative of the broader population, introducing significant selection bias into observational studies. Alternatively, in high burden populations where measles is more common, there persists inequalities in healthcare access which complicates the establishment of reliable cohorts. Working within these restraints, studies have looked at quantifying the increased risk in non-measles infections post-measles-infection, when compared to children who were not sick with measles 4,5 . However, these studies using contemporary individual data cannot link immune amnesia to mortality due to limited cohort sizes and low mortality rates. The claim that measles immune amnesia may have contributed to up to half of all childhood deaths from infectious diseases in the pre-vaccine era, and that following the introduction of vaccination, the subsequent decline in measles infections was the primary driver of reduced childhood infectious disease mortality comes from a paper by Mina et al. These authors measured measles immune amnesia by quantifying the drop in non-measles infectious disease mortality in three countries before and after the introduction of the measles vaccines. This statement does not address mortality fluctuations across history and regions, but in the case of Denmark, the data used to make this claim, comes from when infectious disease mortality was already nearing historic lows. In 1986, the year before the measles vaccine was introduced, there were a total of 19 deaths from non-measles childhood infections, five years later, in 1991, there was a total of 16 deaths. For example, in the early 20 th century in Copenhagen, census data shows childhood mortality is highly concentrated towards the first year of life 6 , well before the average age of measles infection which was estimated to be 5.65 years 7 using weekly measles infection numbers taken from 1907 to 1930. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand the long-term effects of measles on the immune system and mortality, particularly in the context of historical data, as measles prevention is well understood but its impact on immune function and mortality remains contested.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used historical data from Denmark and Switzerland, focusing on individual-level mortality and morbidity records from the pre-vaccination period. It examined measles infections and non-measles infectious disease mortality across different age groups and time periods.
analysis.methods: The authors analyzed historical demographic data and linked measles case records to death certificates to study the long-term consequences of measles infection. They also used statistical models to visualize trends in infectious disease mortality and compared them with measles infection patterns.
analysis.main_results: The study found that measles-induced immune amnesia may have contributed to up to half of all childhood deaths from infectious diseases in the pre-vaccine era. However, the data from Denmark showed that non-measles childhood infections had already reached historic lows before the introduction of the measles vaccine, making the results unsuitable for speculating on the contribution of measles immune amnesia to childhood infectious disease mortality.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that the lack of overlap between the age distribution of measles infections and non-measles deaths suggests that measles immune amnesia was unlikely to be a major contributor to infectious disease mortality in 20th-century Copenhagen. They proposed that historical data offers unique advantages for studying measles effects on the immune system and its long-term consequences.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the importance of using historical data to better understand the impact of measles on the immune system and its role in infectious disease mortality, which can inform future research and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by the inherent unequal distribution of measles infections and the confounding factors in observational settings, such as pre-existing comorbidities and healthcare-seeking behaviors. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations and the reliance on historical data.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores the long-term effects of measles on the immune system and mortality, emphasizing the importance of historical data in understanding these impacts. The authors highlight that while measles prevention is well understood, its effects on immune function and mortality remain contested. They analyzed historical demographic data and linked measles case records to death certificates to study the long-term consequences of measles infection. The study found that measles-induced immune amnesia may have contributed to up to half of all childhood deaths from infectious diseases in the pre-vaccine era, but the data from Denmark showed that non-measles childhood infections had already reached historic lows before the introduction of the measles vaccine, making the results unsuitable for speculating on the contribution of measles immune amnesia to childhood infectious disease mortality. The authors interpreted that the lack of overlap between the age distribution of measles infections and non-measles deaths suggests that measles immune amnesia was unlikely to be a major contributor to infectious disease mortality in 20th-century Copenhagen. They proposed that historical data offers unique advantages for studying measles effects on the immune system and its long-term consequences. The study is limited by the inherent unequal distribution of measles infections and the confounding factors in observational settings, such as pre-existing comorbidities and healthcare-seeking behaviors. The evidence is moderate due to these limitations and the reliance on historical data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解死亡率对免疫系统以及麻疹的长期影响,特别是在历史数据的背景下,因为麻疹的预防措施已被充分理解,但其对免疫功能和死亡率的影响仍存在争议。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了丹麦和瑞士的历史数据,重点关注疫情前时期的个体层面死亡率和发病率记录。它分析了不同年龄组和不同时期的麻疹感染情况以及非麻疹传染病的死亡率情况。
elements_zh.methods: 作者分析了历史人口统计数据,并将麻疹病例记录与死亡证明相联系,以研究麻疹感染的长期后果。他们还使用统计模型来可视化传染性疾病死亡率的趋势,并将其与麻疹感染模式进行比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究发现,麻疹诱导的免疫遗忘可能对疫苗时代前所有儿童感染性疾病死亡的多达一半有所贡献。然而,丹麦的数据表明,在引入麻疹 疫苗之前,非麻疹的儿童感染已经降至历史最低水平,使得这些结果不适合用于推测麻疹免疫遗忘对儿童感染性疾病死亡率的贡献。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,麻疹感染的年龄分布与非麻疹死亡的年龄分布之间缺乏重叠,表明麻疹免疫遗忘不太可能是20世纪哥本哈根传染病死亡率的主要贡献因素。他们提出,历史数据对于研究麻疹对免疫系统的影响及其长期后果具有独特优势。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了利用历史数据以更好地理解死亡率对免疫系统的影响及其在传染性疾病麻疹中的作用,这可以为未来的研究和公共卫生策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到固有的麻疹感染分布不均以及观察性研究中混杂因素的限制,例如先前存在的合并症和就医行为。由于这些限制以及依赖历史数据,证据等级为中等。

Even studies directly comparing vaccinated and unvaccinated children are often affected by substantial confounding, as the two groups may differ systematically with respect to socioeconomic status, access to healthcare, health-seeking behavior, and parental attitudes towards healthcare and vaccination. Integrating historical data is therefore essential to overcome these limitations and to advance our understanding of measles-induced immune amnesia and its long-term consequences.Annual counts of measles infections were reported in four age brackets; under 1, 1-5, 5-15, and 15-65. These totals were fitted to a gamma distribution to show the overall trend.Mortality data was in higher granularity with yearly frequency up until age 5, and then 5-10, 10-15, and 10-20. These totals were fitted with a power law function to show the overall trend. Notably, "infant diarrhea", the most significant source of mortality among under 1s at 286.6 per 10,000 was not included in the death total because it is considered food and water borne.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在了解死亡率对免疫系统以及麻疹的长期影响,特别是在历史数据的背景下,因为麻疹的预防措施已被充分理解,但其对免疫功能和死亡率的影响仍存在争议。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用了丹麦和瑞士的历史数据,重点关注疫情前时期的个体层面死亡率和发病率记录。它分析了不同年龄组和不同时期的麻疹感染情况以及非麻疹传染病的死亡率情况。
analysis_zh.methods: 作者分析了历史人口统计数据,并将麻疹病例记录与死亡证明相联系,以研究麻疹感染的长期后果。他们还使用统计模型来可视化传染性疾病死亡率的趋势,并将其与麻疹感染模式进行比较。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究发现,麻疹诱导的免疫遗忘可能对疫苗时代前所有儿童感染性疾病死亡的多达一半有所贡献。然而,丹麦的数据表明,在引入麻疹 疫苗之前,非麻疹的儿童感染已经降至历史最低水平,使得这些结果不适合用于推测麻疹免疫遗忘对儿童感染性疾病死亡率的贡献。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者认为,麻疹感染的年龄分布与非麻疹死亡的年龄分布之间缺乏重叠,表明麻疹免疫遗忘不太可能是20世纪哥本哈根传染病死亡率的主要贡献因素。他们提出,历史数据对于研究麻疹对免疫系统的影响及其长期后果具有独特优势。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现强调了利用历史数据以更好地理解死亡率对免疫系统的影响及其在传染性疾病麻疹中的作用,这可以为未来的研究和公共卫生策略提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到固有的麻疹感染分布不均以及观察性研究中混杂因素的限制,例如先前存在的合并症和就医行为。由于这些限制以及依赖历史数据,证据等级为中等。

papers.title: Differential Susceptibility of hiPSC-Derived Neural Progenitors and Neurons to Measles Virus Infection Reveals Unique Neuronal Budding and Viral Mutations
papers.abstract: Abstract Measles virus (MeV) can cause severe neurological complications such as measles inclusion body encephalitis (MIBE) and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), but the mechanisms of MeV infection in the human Central Nervous System (CNS) remain poorly understood. In this study, we modeled MeV infection in the CNS using neural progenitor cells (NPC) and cortical neurons derived from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC), evaluating infectivity, viral replication and mutation, and neural function after infection. NPC were highly susceptible and permissive to infection, forming cytoplasmic inclusion bodies, undergoing apoptotic death, but producing infectious particles. In contrast, neurons supported viral replication but did not produce infectious progeny, despite the visualization of budding viral particles by Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM). Our findings advance the understanding of MeV neuropathogenesis and support the utility of hiPSC-derived neural models for studying neurotropic viral infections since we could reproduce key aspects of MeV neuronal infection.

papers.title_zh: hiPSC来源的神经前体细胞和神经元对麻疹病毒感染的差异易感性揭示了独特的神经元芽生和病毒突变
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Measles virus (MeV) can cause severe neurological complications such as measles inclusion body encephalitis (MIBE) and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis (SSPE), but the mechanisms of MeV infection in the human Central Nervous System (CNS) remain poorly understood. In this study, we modeled MeV infection in the CNS using neural progenitor cells (NPC) and cortical neurons derived from human-induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSC), evaluating infectivity, viral replication and mutation, and neural function after infection. NPC were highly susceptible and permissive to infection, forming cytoplasmic inclusion bodies, undergoing apoptotic death, but producing infectious particles. In contrast, neurons supported viral replication but did not produce infectious progeny, despite the visualization of budding viral particles by Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM). Our findings advance the understanding of MeV neuropathogenesis and support the utility of hiPSC-derived neural models for studying neurotropic viral infections since we could reproduce key aspects of MeV neuronal infection.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 麻疹病毒(MeV)可引起严重的神经并发症,如麻疹包涵体脑炎(MIBE)和亚急性硬化性全脑炎(SSPE),但MeV在人类中枢神经系统(CNS)中的感染机制仍不明确。在本研究中,我们利用人类诱导多能干细胞(hiPSC)来源的神经前体细胞(NPC)和皮层神经元模拟MeV在CNS中的感染,评估感染后的感染性、病毒复制和突变以及神经功能。NPC对感染表现出高度易感性和允许性,形成细胞质包涵体,经历凋亡死亡,但能产生感染性颗粒。相比之下,神经元支持病毒复制,但未产生感染性子代,尽管通过传播电子显微镜(TEM)观察到了芽生病毒颗粒。我们的研究结果推进了对MeV神经发病机制的理解,并支持使用hiPSC来源的神经模型来研究神经嗜性病毒感染,因为我们能够再现MeV神经元感染的关键特征。

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to examine the lessons learned from the West Texas measles outbreak regarding public health leadership and response strategies.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary on the West Texas measles outbreak, which occurred in 2026, and focuses on public health leadership and management practices during the event.
analysis.methods: The methods involved a retrospective analysis of public health leadership strategies and outcomes during the West Texas measles outbreak, including case management, communication protocols, and community engagement.
analysis.main_results: The commentary highlights the importance of coordinated leadership, rapid response, and community engagement in mitigating the spread of measles during the outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the outbreak as a case study demonstrating the critical role of effective public health leadership in managing infectious disease outbreaks, offering novel insights into leadership practices.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health leadership training and preparedness for future outbreaks, emphasizing the need for proactive and collaborative strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a commentary and does not include quantitative data, which limits the strength of the evidence but provides valuable qualitative insights.

analysis.summary_en: This commentary reflects on the West Texas measles outbreak of 2026, emphasizing the importance of public health leadership in managing infectious disease crises. The study outlines the challenges faced during the outbreak and highlights the need for coordinated, rapid, and community-focused responses. While the analysis is qualitative and lacks quantitative data, it offers novel insights into leadership practices that can inform future outbreak management. The findings suggest that effective leadership is crucial for controlling measles outbreaks and improving public health preparedness. The study's limitations include its reliance on a narrative rather than empirical data, which affects the strength of the evidence but does not diminish its value as a case study.

elements_en.study_design_and_population: The study is a commentary on the West Texas measles outbreak, which occurred in 2026, and focuses on public health leadership and management practices during the event.
elements_en.methods: The methods involved a retrospective analysis of public health leadership strategies and outcomes during the West Texas measles outbreak, including case management, communication protocols, and community engagement.
elements_en.main_results: The commentary highlights the importance of coordinated leadership, rapid response, and community engagement in mitigating the spread of measles during the outbreak.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret the outbreak as a case study demonstrating the critical role of effective public health leadership in managing infectious disease outbreaks, offering novel insights into leadership practices.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform public health leadership training and preparedness for future outbreaks, emphasizing the need for proactive and collaborative strategies.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on a commentary and does not include quantitative data, which limits the strength of the evidence but provides valuable qualitative insights.

papers.title: Outcome of Measles in Vaccinated versus Unvaccinated Children under 5 years of age
papers.abstract: Objective: To determine the frequency of measles vaccination among children under 5 years of age presenting with measles and to compare the outcomes between vaccinated and unvaccinated children. Outcomes were defined as (i) prolonged hospital admission of two days or more (primary outcome, taken as the marker of severe disease) and (ii) measles-related complications (secondary outcome). Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study was conducted at the Department of Paediatrics, Benazir Bhutto Hospital, Rawalpindi, from October 2025 to December 2025, and reported in accordance with the STROBE guidelines for cross-sectional studies. A total of 150 children aged 1–5 years of either sex were enrolled using non-probability consecutive sampling. Measles was defined by the WHO clinical case definition (fever ≥38 °C with a generalised maculopapular rash lasting ≥3 days, together with at least one of cough, coryza, or conjunctivitis). A child was classified as vaccinated when at least one dose of a measles-containing vaccine given at or after 9 months of age was documented on the Expanded Program on Immunisation (EPI) card, and as unvaccinated when no dose was documented. Children with chickenpox, other skin infections, congenital anomalies, chronic illnesses, immunocompromised status, or incomplete vaccination records were excluded. Groups were compared using the chi-square test, and effect sizes were reported as odds ratios (OR), risk ratios (RR), and absolute risk differences with 95% confidence intervals (CI). Results: The mean age of the children was 3.18 ± 1.21 years, and the mean weight was 12.46 ± 2.84 kg. Of the 150 children, 38 (25.3%) were vaccinated, and 112 (74.7%) were unvaccinated. Prolonged hospital admission was required by 57 of 112 (50.9%) unvaccinated children compared with 10 of 38 (26.3%) vaccinated children (OR 2.90, 95% CI 1.29–6.53; RR 1.93, 95% CI 1.10–3.39; absolute risk difference 24.6%, 95% CI 7.8–41.4; p = 0.009). Complications were observed in 73 (48.7%) children overall, with pneumonia being the most common complication in 34 (22.7%), followed by diarrhoea in 21 (14.0%), otitis media in 10 (6.7%), and encephalitis in 8 (5.3%). The overall frequency of complications did not differ significantly between unvaccinated (55/112, 49.1%) and vaccinated (18/38, 47.4%) children (OR 1.07, 95% CI 0.51–2.24; p = 0.853). Conclusion: Unvaccinated children < 5 years of age with measles had a significantly greater need for prolonged hospital admission than vaccinated children, indicating that measles vaccination attenuates the severity of illness in children who acquire the infection. The overall frequency of complications did not differ significantly between the two groups; this null result should be interpreted cautiously, given the small number of vaccinated children and the correspondingly wide confidence interval. These findings support the need to strengthen routine measles immunisation coverage in children under 5 years of age. Keywords: Measles; Measles Vaccine; Vaccination; Child, Preschool; Hospitalization; Treatment Outcome; Immunization Programs; Pakistan.

Conducted at Benazir Bhutto Hospital in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, from October to December 2025, the descriptive cross-sectional study enrolled 150 children using non-probability consecutive sampling. Measles was defined by the WHO clinical case definition, and vaccination status was determined by EPI card records. papers.title: Measles Risk and MMR Vaccination Timing in Dermatology Patients on Immunosuppressive Therapy
papers.abstract: The 2025-6 measles outbreak marked a significant resurgence of a vaccine-preventable disease, raising urgent public health concerns. The clinical implications of this outbreak for patients on immunosuppressive therapy, specifically in dermatology, remains poorly defined. This review addresses this gap, examining measles presentations and complications in immunosuppressed dermatology patients. We discuss diagnostic considerations specific to this population, in whom impaired humoral immunity can limited the reliability of standard testing. Finally, we propose a practical, dosing and pharmokinetic-based framework for MMR vaccination and post-exposure prophylaxis decisions across commonly used dermatologic therapies. This includes specifically biologics, targeted small molecules, and conventional immunosuppressants. Current public health guidance was largely developed from oncology, transplant, and rheumatology populations, leaving dermatologists without a clear or actionable plan for their patients. This review is intended to fill that gap and serve as a quick reference tool for dermatologists navigating measles risk in the context of immunomodulatory therapy.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于麻疹病毒(人麻疹病毒),历史名称如麻疹和麻疹病,以及相关疾病如亚急性硬化性全脑炎。核心问题是皮肤病患者在接受免疫抑制治疗时面临麻疹的风险,以及该人群在MMR 疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防方面的最佳时机。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述基于2025-6 麻疹 暴发,探讨了免疫抑制皮肤病患者中麻疹的临床表现和并发症。它讨论了针对该人群的特定诊断考虑因素,并强调了皮肤科医生缺乏明确公共卫生指导的现状。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,麻疹对接受免疫抑制治疗的皮肤病患者构成重大风险,由于体液免疫受损,标准诊断检测的可靠性可能受限。它强调了需要为疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防制定个性化的策略。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,目前针对麻疹预防的公共卫生指导主要基于肿瘤学、移植学和风湿病学人群,导致皮肤科医生缺乏针对其患者的明确或可操作的计划。这代表了在免疫抑制治疗皮肤病患者中特定证据的空白。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述提出了一个基于剂量和药代动力学的实用框架,用于在常用的皮肤病治疗方案中做出MMR 疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防决策。其目标是为皮肤科医生在免疫调节治疗背景下管理麻疹风险提供快速参考工具。

This review is intended to fill that gap and serve as a quick reference tool for dermatologists navigating measles risk in the context of immunomodulatory therapy.
papers.abstract_zh: 2025-6 麻疹 暴发标志着一种疫苗可预防疾病的显著回升,引发了紧迫的公共卫生关注。这种暴发对接受免疫抑制治疗的患者,特别是在皮肤病患者中,其临床意义尚未明确。本综述旨在填补这一空白,探讨免疫抑制皮肤病患者中麻疹的临床表现和并发症。我们讨论了针对该人群的特定诊断考虑因素,其中由于体液免疫受损,标准检测的可靠性可能受限。最后,我们提出了一种基于剂量和药代动力学的实用框架,用于在常用的皮肤病治疗方案中做出MMR 疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防决策。这包括特定的生物制剂、靶向小分子药物以及传统免疫抑制剂。目前的公共卫生指导主要基于肿瘤学、移植学和风湿病学人群,使得皮肤科医生缺乏针对其患者的明确或可操作的计划。本综述旨在填补这一空白,并为皮肤科医生在免疫调节治疗背景下管理麻疹风险提供快速参考工具。
papers.summary_zh: 2025-6 麻疹 暴发标志着一种疫苗可预防疾病的显著回升,引发了紧迫的公共卫生关注。这种暴发对接受免疫抑制治疗的患者,特别是在皮肤病患者中,其临床意义尚未明确。本综述旨在填补这一空白,探讨免疫抑制皮肤病患者中麻疹的临床表现和并发症。我们讨论了针对该人群的特定诊断考虑因素,其中由于体液免疫受损,标准检测的可靠性可能受限。最后,我们提出了一种基于剂量和药代动力学的实用框架,用于在常用的皮肤病治疗方案中做出MMR 疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防决策。这包括特定的生物制剂、靶向小分子药物以及传统免疫抑制剂。目前的公共卫生指导主要基于肿瘤学、移植学和风湿病学人群,使得皮肤科医生缺乏针对其患者的明确或可操作的计划。本综述旨在填补这一空白,并为皮肤科医生在免疫调节治疗背景下管理麻疹风险提供快速参考工具。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于麻疹病毒(人麻疹病毒),历史名称如麻疹和麻疹病,以及相关疾病如亚急性硬化性全脑炎。核心问题是皮肤病患者在接受免疫抑制治疗时面临麻疹的风险,以及该人群在MMR 疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防方面的最佳时机。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述基于2025-6 麻疹 暴发,探讨了免疫抑制皮肤病患者中麻疹的临床表现和并发症。它讨论了针对该人群的特定诊断考虑因素,并强调了皮肤科医生缺乏明确公共卫生指导的现状。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,麻疹对接受免疫抑制治疗的皮肤病患者构成重大风险,由于体液免疫受损,标准诊断检测的可靠性可能受限。它强调了需要为疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防制定个性化的策略。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 综述指出,目前针对麻疹预防的公共卫生指导主要基于肿瘤学、移植学和风湿病学人群,导致皮肤科医生缺乏针对其患者的明确或可操作的计划。这代表了在免疫抑制治疗皮肤病患者中特定证据的空白。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述提出了一个基于剂量和药代动力学的实用框架,用于在常用的皮肤病治疗方案中做出MMR 疫苗接种接种和暴露后预防决策。其目标是为皮肤科医生在免疫调节治疗背景下管理麻疹风险提供快速参考工具。

OffOn Stream on US measles cases surpass 2,000 for the 2nd year in a row: CDC So far this year, 2,030 cases have been recorded in 38 states and D.C. ByMary Kekatos and Georgia Davis June 5, 2026, 6:07 PM Share Measles cases in the United States have surpassed 2,000 for the second year in a row, according to data updated Friday from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). So far in 2026, 2,030 confirmed cases have been recorded in 38 states and the District of Columbia, CDC data shows. Cases have been confirmed in: Alaska, Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Kansas, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island, South Carolina, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, Wisconsin and Wyoming. Related 1 year since measles cases found in Texas, US still seeing surge of infections with elimination status at risk Just 10 measles cases were reported among international travelers so far this year, according to CDC data. Last year, 2,288 confirmed measles cases were reported for all of 2025. Prior to this, measles cases had not surpassed 2,000 in the U.S. since 1992. The U.S. also saw its first measles deaths in more than a decade last year, including two among unvaccinated school-aged children in Texas and one among an unvaccinated adult in New Mexico. The measles virus. BSIP/Universal Images Group via Getty Images The majority of measles cases in 2026 have been confirmed among children and teenagers aged 19 and younger, according to the CDC. About 92% of cases are among people who are unvaccinated or whose vaccination status is unknown, CDC data shows. Meanwhile, 4% of cases are among those who have received just one dose of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine and 4% of cases are among those who received the recommended two doses, according to the CDC. Dr. William Schaffner, a professor of preventive medicine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, referred to the latest figures as "very disappointing and very concerning." "It indicates that an increasing number of parents are either postponing or withholding their children from vaccination, and this is very concerning because it permits this virus back now into in the United States to continue to spread and obviously to cause illness in the children affected," he told ABC News. Related Amid growing Texas outbreak, how contagious is measles? January 2026 marked one year since measles cases were first detected on Texas. It’s unclear if the cases confirmed on Jan. 20, 2025, are linked to those that have been found other states; if so, it would mean the U.S. has seen a year of continuous transmission. Popular Reads Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after botched execution: Attorneys 2 hours ago Iran live updates: Trump says war will be over 'very soon,' but offers no details 2 days ago District attorney reopens case of alleged Cornell University 'gang rape' Sep 29 If it's determined that the U.S. has experienced 12 months of continuous measles transmission, it could lead to a loss of the country's elimination status that was earned in 2000. Measles would once again be considered endemic or constantly circulating. The review of the measles elimination status in the U.S., which is determined by the Pan-American Health Organization, will take place in November 2026. Schaffner said the U.S.'s measles elimination status is threatened as a result of so many cases. "Measles, because it's the most contagious virus, is like the canary in the coal mine; it's the alert that lets us know that we're also opening ourselves up to other transmissible diseases that vaccines could prevent," he said. Related New map shows how to spot the measles risk level in your ZIP code The CDC currently recommends that people receive two doses of the MMR vaccine, the first at ages 12 to 15 months and the second between 4 and 6 years old. One dose is 93% effective, and two doses are 97% effective against measles, the CDC says. However, CDC data show vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2024 to 2025 school year, 92.5% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 92.7% seen the previous school year and the 95.2% seen in the 2019 to 2020 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. Schaffner said that public health specialists need to listen carefully to parents who are skeptical or hesitant of getting their children vaccinated. "Have them speak to their own family doctors and pediatricians, have those conversations, and our pediatricians and family doctors have to provide a level of comfort and reassurance," he said. "Facts are fundamental, but more importantly, these parents need reassurance and a level of comfort that what their doctors ... are recommending is in the best interest of their child and the communities in which their children live." "These diseases are bad and can be really bad. The vaccines are good and really good," Schaffner added. analysis.brief_en: In 2026, the United States has recorded 2,030 confirmed measles cases across 38 states and the District of Columbia, marking the second consecutive year that cases have surpassed 2,000. The CDC reports that the majority of these cases—92%—are among individuals who are unvaccinated or have an unknown vaccination status. This surge has raised concerns about the country's measles elimination status, which was achieved in 2000. If the U.S. experiences 12 months of continuous measles transmission, it could lose its elimination status and the virus may become endemic again. The CDC is preparing for a review of the elimination status in November 2026. Public health experts, including William Schaffner from Vanderbilt University Medical Center, have expressed alarm over the trend, noting that it reflects a growing number of parents delaying or refusing vaccinations for their children. Schaffner emphasized the importance of addressing vaccine hesitancy through informed conversations with healthcare providers to ensure the safety of children and communities.

If the U.S. experiences 12 months of continuous measles transmission, it could lose its elimination status and the virus may become endemic again. The CDC is preparing for a review of the elimination status in November 2026. Public health experts, including William Schaffner from Vanderbilt University Medical Center, have expressed alarm over the trend, noting that it reflects a growing number of parents delaying or refusing vaccinations for their children. Schaffner emphasized the importance of addressing vaccine hesitancy through informed conversations with healthcare providers to ensure the safety of children and communities.

OffOn Stream on Pennsylvania surpasses 900 measles cases with 13 new confirmed infections: Officials At least 176 people have been hospitalized so far. ByMary Kekatos September 28, 2026, 7:08 PM At least 13 new measles cases have been confirmed in Pennsylvania since Friday, bringing the total so far this year to 903, according to Monday's update from the state health department. Cases have been recorded in 39 of Pennsylvania's 67 counties. At least 176 people have been hospitalized, and four measles-associated deaths have been reported, the Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) said. Two of the deaths were among unvaccinated adults: an 18-year-old and a 40-year-old. The other two deaths were among infants who were too young to have received the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine. Related Possible measles exposure at Busch Stadium, local St. Louis-area businesses, officials warn Fewer than 1% of the state's cases -- four in total -- are among those who are fully vaccinated with the MMR vaccine, according to DOH. The majority of cases are among those between ages 25 and 49, followed by those between ages 18 and 24, according to state health department data. The measles virus. BSIP/Universal Images Group via Getty Images Lancaster County in southeastern Pennsylvania has recorded the highest number of cases at 363 followed by Mifflin County, in the central part of the state, with 105. At least 11 counties show evidence of community transmission, which is when infectious illness spreads through a local population without any known travel history and the specific source of infection cannot be determined. DOH data shows staff have administered more than 8,300 doses of the MMR vaccine so far this year. Uptake was highest in August with about 3,500 vaccine doses administered, followed by September with about 2,500 doses administered. Popular Reads Tennessee is set to execute a woman for the first time in 200 years Sep 28 Iran live updates: Trump says war will be over 'very soon,' but offers no details 2 days ago Tel Aviv flight drops thousands of feet after pilot stabbed in alleged terror attack Sep 30 Meanwhile, measles cases in the U.S. have surpassed 3,600 so far in 2026, with cases confirmed in 45 states and Washington, D.C., according to the latest data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. The CDC has reported one death from measles so far this year but did not say where the death occurred. A note on the agency's website said the number "is subject to change." The CDC currently recommends that people receive two doses of the MMR vaccine, the first at ages 12 to 15 months and the second between 4 and 6 years old. Infants who are between 6 and 11 months old and traveling outside of the country may require an additional vaccination. One dose is 93% effective in preventing measles infection and two doses are 97% effective, the CDC says. Related How hospitals, clinics in Pennsylvania are responding to the measles outbreak However, CDC data shows vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2025 to 2026 school year, 92.4% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 95.2% seen in the 2019 to 2020 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. "If you've been exposed, it is important to talk to a healthcare professional, but don't go into an urgent care or an ER because you may be inevitably spreading it to other vulnerable people," ABC News medical contributor Dr. Alok Patel told "ABC News Live" on Friday. "People who have been exposed may be instructed to quarantine or keep really close eye on their symptoms for up to 21 days because that's how long it can really take for measles to show itself and you could potentially spread and infect others without even knowing it," Patel added. At least 176 people have been hospitalized, and four measles-associated deaths have been reported, the Pennsylvania Department of Health (DOH) said. Two of the deaths were among unvaccinated adults: an 18-year-old and a 40-year-old. The other two deaths were among infants who were too young to have received the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine. Related Possible measles exposure at Busch Stadium, local St. Louis-area businesses, officials warn Fewer than 1% of the state's cases -- four in total -- are among those who are fully vaccinated with the MMR vaccine, according to DOH. The majority of cases are among those between ages 25 and 49, followed by those between ages 18 and 24, according to state health department data. The measles virus. BSIP/Universal Images Group via Getty Images Lancaster County in southeastern Pennsylvania has recorded the highest number of cases at 363 followed by Mifflin County, in the central part of the state, with 105. At least 11 counties show evidence of community transmission, which is when infectious illness spreads through a local population without any known travel history and the specific source of infection cannot be determined. DOH data shows staff have administered more than 8,300 doses of the MMR vaccine so far this year. Uptake was highest in August with about 3,500 vaccine doses administered, followed by September with about 2,500 doses administered. The CDC has reported one death from measles so far this year but did not say where the death occurred. A note on the agency's website said the number "is subject to change." The CDC currently recommends that people receive two doses of the MMR vaccine, the first at ages 12 to 15 months and the second between 4 and 6 years old. Infants who are between 6 and 11 months old and traveling outside of the country may require an additional vaccination. One dose is 93% effective in preventing measles infection and two doses are 97% effective, the CDC says. Related How hospitals, clinics in Pennsylvania are responding to the measles outbreak However, CDC data shows vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2025 to 2026 school year, 92.4% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 95.2% seen in the 2019 to 2020 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. "If you've been exposed, it is important to talk to a healthcare professional, but don't go into an urgent care or an ER because you may be inevitably spreading it to other vulnerable people," ABC News medical contributor Dr. Alok Patel told "ABC News Live" on Friday. "People who have been exposed may be instructed to quarantine or keep really close eye on their symptoms for up to 21 days because that's how long it can really take for measles to show itself and you could potentially spread and infect others without even knowing it," Patel added. news.content: Follow this section to personalize your feed and get instant alerts. Update your preferences in Account Settings Follow this tag to personalize your feed and get instant alerts. Follow this author to personalize your feed and get instant alerts. Essential insights into the unfolding AI revolution. This fall in the U.S., as kids settle into a new school year, measles is spreading at a level not seen in 35 years . Children have died. And in just the past month, 10 children have been infected in an outbreak linked to a single daycare in Georgia. Far too many students are entering classrooms vulnerable to a highly contagious and dangerous virus. Yet there has been relative silence from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), the agency where I once served as a senior leader, about measles. CDC’s back-to-school messages on X have advised families about sleep, physical activity, healthy lunches, and bullying. All are important. But one message emphasized in prior years at the start of school is noticeably absent and can now be found only in CDC’s online archives : Get your child up to date on routine vaccinations. During the country’s largest measles resurgence in decades, that should be the nation’s most urgent back-to-school message. CDC’s reticence extends beyond social media. Four measles-associated deaths reported by Pennsylvania were initially absent from the agency’s national dashboard . In late August, CDC posted two of the Pennsylvania deaths, then added an asterisk and language that it was reviewing additional information. The deaths were later removed without a clear explanation. Now two deaths are reported on CDC’s dashboard as of September 28 without identifying the states. This is not transparency; it is silence at a moment when families need clear, accurate information to protect their children. Why are these deaths being left off the official tally? There’s a disagreement between federal and state officials over how to count measles deaths—even though Pennsylvania investigated each death and reported them to CDC through the established nationally notifiable disease surveillance system that has been used by state and local health departments across the country for years. In late August, when officials from Pennsylvania announced the first two deaths there, Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS), even questioned if the deaths were fabricated. But Pennsylvania’s definition of a measles-associated death ensures that deaths unrelated to underlying measles infection are not counted . Leaders at HHS and CDC have said they are working to clearly define measles deaths and that it will update its counts as reviews are complete. But the agency has not explained which deaths they are currently counting, how these decisions are being made, why the data reporting system used by states was changed, and how they will account for the secondary infections and other complications caused by measles .Two former leaders of the National Center for Health Statistics have called this out publicly, writing in STAT that these changes will delay reporting and add to public confusion about the severity of measles. An important question to ask is whether shifting explanations and new disease-classification systems are clarifying the outbreak or miring it in confusion and making it easier to minimize. A single measles case can expose dozens of classmates, teachers, and siblings, as well as infants too young to be vaccinated. Federal officials should be using their platforms to prevent the next case and not debating the numbers. Meanwhile, the big picture is being missed: We know how to prevent this. After the last significant measles surge in the late 1980s, the CDC Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices and the American Academy of Pediatrics recommended that all kids receive a second dose of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine at age four to six. One dose is approximately 93% effective against measles; two doses are approximately 97% effective . But national MMR coverage among kindergartners fell again during the 2025-2026 school year, and approximately 280,000 kindergartners attended school without documentation that they had completed the MMR series. Vaccine exemptions in 24 states exceeded 5% , meaning these communities no longer have the 95% adequate protection to keep measles from spreading. The impact extends beyond the child who becomes sick. When an unvaccinated student is exposed to measles, they will often be required to stay at home for at least 21 days. That means missed academics, missed social interactions, and missed work for parents. In addition to the impact on a child and their family, each case of measles costs the public-health system on average $58,600 to respond to , including the cost of contact tracing and quarantines. And measles isn’t over when the rash goes away. It can result in “ immune amnesia ,” meaning kids are more likely to get other infections over the next two to three years , and approximately one in 10,000 people who recovered from measles will die years later from the rare brain disease subacute sclerosing panencephalitis. Amid the recent deadly outbreaks of measles, our federal health leaders have too often paired a lukewarm recommendation to vaccinate with insinuations and incorrect information about vaccine ingredients, fetal tissue, or waning immunity . The same week families needed clarity about a growing outbreak, Kennedy addressed a conference hosted by Children’s Health Defense, the anti-vaccine organization he once led . In response to the outbreak, Pennsylvania has opened up nearly 150 pop-up vaccination clinics in homes and community centers, engaged health systems and local clinics across the state, requested federal support for additional vaccinations, developed a dashboard showing community transmission by county, and worked with coroners to investigate deaths . This is boots-on-the-ground public health. Our federal health leaders should reinforce that work rather than cast doubt on it, giving parents and schools clear guidance and reporting cases consistently and transparently. Data and definitions matter, but we cannot lose sight of the people who are behind each of these data points. Each case number represents someone who became sick, and behind each death is a grieving family and a life that deserves to be counted. Now that children are back in school, our responsibility is both simple and urgent: to use the tools we know work to keep this preventable disease out of the classroom. analysis.time: As children return to school in the U.S. this fall, measles is spreading at a level not seen in 35 years (N5). In just the past month, 10 children were infected in an outbreak linked to a single daycare in Georgia (N6).
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak is occurring in the U.S., specifically in Georgia, where 10 children were infected. The affected population includes unvaccinated children and their families, with approximately 280,000 kindergartners attending school without completed MMR series documentation (N32).
analysis.event: Measles is spreading at a level not seen in 35 years, with an outbreak linked to a daycare in Georgia resulting in 10 child infections (N5, N6). The CDC has not emphasized vaccination as a key back-to-school message, despite its importance in preventing measles (N11).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Measles-associated deaths were initially absent from the CDC’s national dashboard but were later reported as of September 28 without identifying the states (N17). Each measles case costs the public-health system an average of $58,600, including contact tracing and quarantines (N37). The disease can lead to immune amnesia and subacute sclerosing panencephalitis, which is a rare brain disease (N39).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The CDC has not provided clear explanations for the changes in how measles deaths are counted, nor has it clarified the criteria for inclusion (N25). Pennsylvania has taken proactive measures by opening pop-up vaccination clinics and developing a dashboard for community transmission (N42).

OffOn Stream on Measles cases in 2026 are set to surpass last year's total. Here's why Last year saw the highest number of measles cases in more than 30 years. ByMary Kekatos July 16, 2026, 12:29 AM Share Follow ABC News on Google The number of reported measles cases in the United States this year is soon set to surpass the total reported for all of last year. Data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shows the U.S. has reported 2,231 cases as of July 9, which is just 58 shy of the 2,289 cases reported for the entirety of 2025. Previously, the 2025 total was the highest number of cases seen in more than 30 years, and some public health specialists believe the U.S. is on track to lose the elimination status it earned in 2000. Related A teen girl's harrowing journey with measles highlights how serious the virus can be for the immunocompromised The specialists told ABC News that there are several reasons for the U.S. breaking measles case records for the second year in a row, including declining vaccination rates, people not fearing the measles virus, a loss of trust in public health institutions and a perceived lack of clear guidance and communication from the nation's top public health officials. "A world leading public health triumph, the elimination of measles in the United States, which was a beacon to the rest of the world, showing that this actually could be done, is eroding, and we are trying to turn back the clock as a society to the bad old days, I'm afraid," Dr. William Schaffner, a professor of preventive medicine at Vanderbilt University Medical Center in Nashville, told ABC News. Not fearing measles In the decade before the measles vaccine became available, the CDC estimates that 3 to 4 million in the U.S. were sickened by measles every year, about 48,000 were hospitalized and about 400 to 500 people died. About 1,000 people suffer encephalitis every year. In 1971, the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine became available and, in 1989, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the American Academy of Pediatrics and the American Academy of Family Physicians recommended that children receive a second MMR dose. In this Feb. 6, 2026, file photo, a sign is shown outside a mobile clinic offering measles and flu vaccinations in Spartanburg, South Carolina. Sean Rayford/Getty Images, FILE By 2000, annual recorded cases had fallen to just 85, and measles was declared eliminated, meaning it was without continuous spread for at least 12 months. The CDC recommends two doses of the MMR vaccine. One dose is 93% effective, and two doses are 97% effective against measles, the CDC says. However, CDC data show vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2024-2025 school year, 92.5% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 92.7% seen in the previous school year and the 95.2% seen in the 2019-2020 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. Dr. Paul Offit, director of the Vaccine Education Center and an attending physician in the division of infectious diseases at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, told ABC News that vaccines are a victim of their own success. Because vaccines were so effective at eliminating measles, many members of the public no longer remember a time when measles was ubiquitous, he said. In turn, some people no longer fear the illness and some focus has shifted to the perceived risks of the vaccines themselves, leading to a decline in vaccination rates. "We don't fear these diseases," Offit said. "Not only do [people] not see these diseases, they didn't grow up with these diseases. So, they're just not scared of the diseases. ... I've had residents in our hospital come up and tell me when we had admitted a case of measles; they'd never seen a case with measles before in their life. That's the problem. You don't fear the disease." Related Amid growing Texas outbreak, how contagious is measles? Declining trust in public health Schaffner said another reason has been a loss of trust in public health and health care professionals since the COVID-19 pandemic. The CDC and other federal public health agencies faced criticism for mixed messaging and unclear guidance during the pandemic, as well as for failing to communicate that guidance was often changing because the pandemic was a fast-evolving situation. "There's been in our society a real diminution of trust in authority, authority of all kinds," Schaffner said, "And so, when professional organizations and governmental organizations such as the CDC recommend vaccines universally, such as measles vaccines, that's greeted with skepticism rather than, when I was growing up, those kinds of pronouncements from professional groups and the CDC would be embraced by my parents and say, 'That's the right thing to do.'" Popular Reads Christa Pike unconscious and on ventilator after botched execution: Attorneys 2 hours ago Tel Aviv flight drops thousands of feet after pilot stabbed in alleged terror attack Sep 30 District attorney reopens case of alleged Cornell University 'gang rape' Sep 29 The rise in distrust has been coupled with a rise in unverified or untrue claims about measles spreading online and on social media, Schaffner said. This includes claims that measles is a harmless virus. One year-old River Jacobs is held by his mother, Caitlin Fuller, while he receives an MMR vaccine from Raynard Covarrubio, at a vaccine clinic put on by Lubbock Public Health Department on March 1, 2025 in Lubbock, Texas. Jan Sonnenmair/Getty Images "Measles was a universal infection of children growing up, but that does not mean it was a trivial infection," Schaffner said. "Quite to the contrary, from the point of view of individual children, it often made them miserable for a week and a half." He went on, "Even more importantly, it is associated with all kinds of complications, middle ear infections, which require more medical care, and pneumonia. This virus could get down into your bronchial tubes and lungs, which causes difficulty breathing, requiring hospitalization, intensive care unit admission, and resulting in some of the deaths." Perceived lack of CDC response As the number of measles cases began rising last year, fueled by a fast-growing outbreak in Texas, both the CDC and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. faced criticism for their alleged silence. A December 2025 analysis from Johns Hopkins University published in the journal Vaccine looked at posts from the CDC's official Facebook, Instagram and X accounts related to measles and the MMR vaccine as well as posts from major news outlets. The analysis found that between Jan. 1, 2025, and Aug. 1, 2025, the CDC posted just 10 times across the three platforms, a decrease from an average of 45.8 posts over the same period from 2021 to 2024, despite fewer measles cases during those years. Related New map shows how to spot the measles risk level in your ZIP code Meanwhile, Kennedy did not endorse the MMR vaccine until an April 6, 2025, X post after meeting with the families of two school-aged children who died of measles in Texas. Data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) shows the U.S. has reported 2,231 cases as of July 9, which is just 58 shy of the 2,289 cases reported for the entirety of 2025. Not fearing measles In the decade before the measles vaccine became available, the CDC estimates that 3 to 4 million in the U.S. were sickened by measles every year, about 48,000 were hospitalized and about 400 to 500 people died. About 1,000 people suffer encephalitis every year. In 1971, the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine became available and, in 1989, the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the American Academy of Pediatrics and the American Academy of Family Physicians recommended that children receive a second MMR dose. In this Feb. 6, 2026, file photo, a sign is shown outside a mobile clinic offering measles and flu vaccinations in Spartanburg, South Carolina. Sean Rayford/Getty Images, FILE By 2000, annual recorded cases had fallen to just 85, and measles was declared eliminated, meaning it was without continuous spread for at least 12 months. The CDC recommends two doses of the MMR vaccine. One dose is 93% effective, and two doses are 97% effective against measles, the CDC says. However, CDC data show vaccination rates have been lagging in recent years. During the 2024-2025 school year, 92.5% of kindergartners received the MMR vaccine, according to data. This is lower than the 92.7% seen in the previous school year and the 95.2% seen in the 2019-2020 school year, prior to the COVID-19 pandemic. Dr. Paul Offit, director of the Vaccine Education Center and an attending physician in the division of infectious diseases at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, told ABC News that vaccines are a victim of their own success. Because vaccines were so effective at eliminating measles, many members of the public no longer remember a time when measles was ubiquitous, he said. In turn, some people no longer fear the illness and some focus has shifted to the perceived risks of the vaccines themselves, leading to a decline in vaccination rates. "We don't fear these diseases," Offit said. "Not only do [people] not see these diseases, they didn't grow up with these diseases. So, they're just not scared of the diseases. ... I've had residents in our hospital come up and tell me when we had admitted a case of measles; they'd never seen a case with measles before in their life. That's the problem. You don't fear the disease." Related Amid growing Texas outbreak, how contagious is measles? The CDC and other federal public health agencies faced criticism for mixed messaging and unclear guidance during the pandemic, as well as for failing to communicate that guidance was often changing because the pandemic was a fast-evolving situation. "There's been in our society a real diminution of trust in authority, authority of all kinds," Schaffner said, "And so, when professional organizations and governmental organizations such as the CDC recommend vaccines universally, such as measles vaccines, that's greeted with skepticism rather than, when I was growing up, those kinds of pronouncements from professional groups and the CDC would be embraced by my parents and say, 'That's the right thing to do.'" analysis_zh.event: 文章报道称,2026年美国麻疹病例数预计将超过2025年全年的总病例数。这一趋势已由CDC数据确认,截至2026年7月9日,美国已报告2,231例病例,仅比2025年的2,289例少58例。该事件是一项确认的公共卫生趋势。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: As of July 9, 2026, 2,231 measles cases have been reported in the U.S. This is close to the 2,289 cases reported in 2025, which was the highest number in over 30 years. The CDC estimates that 3 to 4 million people were sickened by measles annually before the vaccine became available, with 48,000 hospitalized and 400 to 500 deaths. The article also mentions a perceived lack of clear guidance and communication from public health officials, which may affect public perception and response.
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: CDC和卫生与公众服务部部长罗伯特·F·肯尼迪因对麻疹病例上升的沉默而受到批评。CDC在社交媒体上的活动显著减少,从2025年1月1日到文章发表时,仅发布了10条相关内容。文章还提到,一些公共卫生专家认为,美国正面临失去其麻疹根除状态的风险,该状态是在2000年实现的。

news.wechat_summary_zh: 时间：The article was published on 2026-10-02.；地点与对象：The United States is the location.；事件：The article reports that measles cases in 2026 are set to surpass the total reported for all of 2025.；影响与风险：As of July 9， 2026， 2，231 measles cases have been reported in the U.S.；应对与不确定性：The CDC and Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F.

analysis.time: Measles outbreaks could leave thousands vulnerable to infectious diseases for years Liz Szabo The measles virus kills crucial immune cells, putting survivors at risk of being reinfected with diseases they’ve already had.
analysis.event: Measles outbreaks have been reported, with the US having 3,886 confirmed infections and Pennsylvania nearing 1,000 cases. The measles virus is linked to increased vulnerability to infectious diseases due to its impact on immune cells.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The measles infection rate in Jerusalem was 15 times higher than in the rest of Israel during the outbreak.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: CIDRAP reports on measles outbreaks and their implications, including the risk of long-term vulnerability. The US and Pennsylvania are experiencing significant measles cases, and the situation is under ongoing public health monitoring.

analysis.brief_en: CIDRAP reports that measles outbreaks in the United States have reached over 3,886 confirmed infections, with Pennsylvania nearing 1,000 cases. The article highlights that the measles virus can kill crucial immune cells, leaving survivors vulnerable to re-infection with diseases they have already had. In Jerusalem, the measles infection rate was 15 times higher than in the rest of Israel during the outbreak. These findings underscore the potential long-term health risks associated with measles outbreaks. The report emphasizes the need for continued public health monitoring and awareness, as the virus poses a significant threat to immune health. The information is based on confirmed cases and expert analysis, with no evidence of hard exclusions or unrelated entities affecting the findings.

Donn Jones By Nikki Ross – Reporter, Nashville Business Journal Sep 29, 2026 JavaScript is disabled To continue reading this content, please enable JavaScript in your browser settings and refresh this page. Listen to this article 3 min Story Highlights What's This? Saravir Biopharma licensed Vanderbilt Health's measles antibodies for clinical development. The United States reported 3,659 confirmed measles cases across 47 states. The antibody treatment targets pregnant women, infants and immunocompromised people. One of Vanderbilt Health’s antibodies has been picked up by a California company for the next stage of development amid a rapid rise in cases nationwide. Saravir Biopharma Inc. has licensed the health system’s antibodies that could potentially neutralize the measles virus, and is now looking for funding for further development and clinical testing, according to the health system. If the company can obtain the funding, it could have the first monoclonal antibody therapy for the highly infectious respiratory virus in 18 months to two years. “We fast-tracked this research to discover human antibodies for measles virus because of the emerging outbreaks of infections,” said Dr. James Crowe Jr., director of the Vanderbilt Center for Antibody Therapeutics, in a press release. As of Sept. 24, there were 3,659 confirmed measles cases this year, 95% of which are from outbreaks, in the United States across 47 states, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention — the most cases reported since 1990. So far this year, there have been 40 new outbreaks of measles. In 2025 there were 48 total outbreaks, up 200% from the 16 outbreaks reported in 2024. The uptick in outbreaks is from a decline in vaccination rates, according to Vanderbilt Health. Last month, the Pennsylvania Department of Health reported two measles-associated deaths in unvaccinated people, the first such fatalities in 35 years. Since then, two more deaths have been reported by the state. “This could skyrocket into a huge problem,” said Dr. Ron Moss, Saravir Biopharma president and CEO, in the release. The antibody treatment is meant for those who cannot safely receive the vaccine, according to Vanderbilt Health. This includes pregnant women, infants under 12 months of age and immunocompromised people. Moss said these people are the focus of Saravir Biopharma’s anti-measles antibody development program. “Two years [to the clinic] is a conservative estimate,” Moss said in the release. “When we get the funding, we think that timeline could be expedited considerably.” Vanderbilt’s Vaccine Center, also run by Crowe and made up of a team of roughly 50 researchers, has had seven antibodies turned into vaccines for people, including Covid-19, Rift Valley Fever virus, Marburg virus, Enterovirus D68 and Chikungunya.
